trials.role: SPARC: satraplatin plus prednisone vs placebo plus prednisone
trials.outcome: Progression-free survival favored satraplatin (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.57–0.77). Overall survival showed no significant improvement (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.84–1.15). Myelosuppression and gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent with satraplatin than with placebo.

The MTD was 140 mg/m²/day. Thrombocytopenia and neutropenia were dose limiting. Recommended phase II doses were 100 mg/m²/day after prior therapy and 120 mg/m²/day without prior therapy, on days 1–5 every 28 days.

trials.role: Oral JM216 in Japanese patients with advanced solid tumors
trials.outcome: The MTD was 120 mg/m²/day, with 100 mg/m²/day recommended on the 5-day schedule. Dose-limiting events included leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia and diarrhea.

trials.role: Oral satraplatin fed/fasted crossover PK at 80 mg/m²/day
trials.outcome: Seventeen patients were treated, with no dose-limiting toxicity during the first cycle. The PK crossover compared fasting with a high-fat meal.

trials.role: Oral satraplatin PK by baseline renal function at 80 mg/m²/day
trials.outcome: Thirty-two patients were enrolled. Moderate and severe renal impairment increased platinum exposure. No dose-limiting toxicity was observed at this dose in the study.

trials.role: Oral JM216 in adults on a 14-day schedule
trials.outcome: 46 treated and 15 in the PK analysis. Delayed neutropenia was dose limiting. MTDs were 45 and 50 mg/m²/day for patients with extensive and limited/no prior treatment, respectively. The phase II doses stated in the Results and abstract were 40 and 45 mg/m²/day on days 1–14 every 5 weeks.

trials.role: Oral satraplatin in children and young adults with refractory solid tumors
trials.outcome: Nine treated and seven in the PK analysis. MTD was 60 mg/m²/dose on days 1–5 every 28 days. Delayed myelosuppression was dose limiting in two of four patients at 80 mg/m²/dose.

trials.role: Veterinary dose escalation in dogs with spontaneous malignant tumors
trials.outcome: Twenty-three dogs received oral satraplatin. The MTD was 35 mg/m²/day on days 1–5 every 3–4 weeks. Myelosuppression was dose limiting. In the 35 mg/m²/day cohort (15 dogs), cycle 1 grade 3–4 neutropenia occurred in 3 dogs and grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia in 2.

trials.role: Single-dose oral JM216 dose escalation in adults
trials.outcome: Thirty-seven patients received 88 courses with single oral doses of 60–700 mg/m² every 3–4 weeks. MTD was not reached. Escalation stopped because of nonlinear PK. Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia were variable at 420–700 mg/m².

trials.role: Oral satraplatin with concurrent thoracic irradiation for NSCLC
trials.outcome: The investigators reported an MTD of 40 mg/day (fixed dose) on radiotherapy days, five days/week for seven weeks, with concurrent 63 Gy. The two patients at 40 mg/day had grade 3 liver function test elevation or gastrointestinal toxicity with fever. The recommended dose for the combined regimen was 30 mg/day.

trials.role: Renal safety study of oral JM216 in patients with lung cancer
trials.outcome: After the first cycle (120 mg/m²/day for 5 days), 20 paired assessments showed no significant acute impairment of renal function. Median GFR was 101 before treatment and 117 mL/min afterwards, ERPF 417 and 418 mL/min, and filtration fraction 0.25 and 0.28. Four patients assessed after 3–6 cycles had no significant impairment. Six patients with small-cell lung cancer escalated to 140 mg/m²/day after the first cycle.

logp.method_description: The determination of the partition coefficients of target complexes using the classic n-octanol/water shake-flask method can be summarized as follows: First, equal volumes of n-octanol and purified water were mixed and shaken at 37°C for 24 h to allow mutual saturation of the two phases. After standing for 1 h, the phases were separated for later use. The complexes were dissolved in water-saturated n-octanol to prepare solutions at concentrations of 40, 60, 80, 100, and 120 μM. The absorbance of each concentration was measured in triplicate using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer, and the average values were used to construct a standard curve to ensure reliable linearity. Subsequently, n-octanol-saturated aqueous solution was placed in a centrifuge tube, and the target complex was added to prepare a 50 μM test sample. The mixture was shaken at 37°C for 48 h to ensure equilibrium distribution. After standing for 1 h, the phases were completely separated by centrifugation at 2500 rpm for 15 min. The solutions from both phases were sampled using syringes, and their absorbance values were measured in triplicate using a UV–Vis spectrophotometer. The average values were used for subsequent concentration calculations. The lipid phase concentration (Co) was calculated based on the standard curve, and the aqueous phase concentration (Cw) was determined using the principle of mass conservation. The LogPo/w of the complex was calculated using Equation (1): log Po/w = log(Co / Cw)

Lipophilicity was determined as the partition coefficient between n-octanol and water (log P o/w) and as the chromatographic retention factor (log k w). The log P o/w determination was carried out according to the OECD guidelines for the classical shake flask method [23] with slight modifications. The complexes were dissolved in Milli-Q water (pre-saturated with 1-octanol) and the platinum concentration was determined by ICP-MS. The remaining stock solution was mixed with an equal volume of 1-octanol (pre-saturated with Milli-Q water) and shaken for 1 h. After phase separation, the platinum concentration was again determined in the aqueous phase by ICP-MS and the partition coefficients were calculated assuming the missing quantity (compared to the stock solution) in the organic phase. ICP-MS measurements were carried out after dilution of the samples with 1 % HNO3 using the instrumental parameters given in Table 1.

The hydrophobicity (log P) of the series of compounds was determined using a shake-flask method (Albert, 1979). Aqueous (0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride (NaCl) and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. Drugs were dissolved at a final concentration of 300 µM in the aqueous phase. An equal volume of saturated noctanol was added and the solutions mixed for 30 min (45 rpm). Samples were centrifuged (1500 g, 10 min) and the platinum content of the organic and aqueous phases determined by ICP-MS. The log of the ratio of platinum concentrations in the organic and aqueous phases were calculated to determine log P.

The equal volume of octanol and purified water were mixed and shaken in a shaker for 24 h for pre-saturated solution treatment. The equal volume pre-treated n-octanol and aqueous solution were precisely measured and mixed, and the tested complex was slowly added to the solution until saturated, then shaken in a shaker for 48 h, and centrifuged at 2500 r/min for 15 min. The absorbance of the two-phase solution was measured by UV–Vis, and log Pow was calculated by formula (4-1). Ao was the UV absorbance value of the complex in the lipid phase (n-octanol) at a specific wavelength, and Aw was the UV absorbance value of the complex in the water phase at the corresponding wavelength. logPow = log(Ao/Aw)
